caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This grouped bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, with error bars representing standard deviation. The horizontal axis displays nine language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, arranged from left to right in that order. The vertical axis, labeled "effect," is scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Six model configurations are compared: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light red), and XLM-B2 (dark red), as indicated in the legend on the right. Each language family has a group of six bars, one for each model, arranged in the order specified by the legend. The IE-Indic family shows the highest overall effects, with bars reaching approximately 20–25 for most models (e.g., mBERT-R2 ≈ 20, XLM-R2 ≈ 18, mBERT-B2 ≈ 24, XLM-B2 ≈ 21). The Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects for all models, with bars mostly at or near 0. The IE-Germanic family shows consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all models; for example, XLM-B2 reaches approximately 20 in IE-Germanic versus around 6 in IE-Romance. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 ≈ 17, XLM-B2 ≈ 16) are substantially higher than the L2 (mBERT-L2 ≈ 10, XLM-L2 ≈ 9) and R2 (mBERT-R2 ≈ 2, XLM-R2 ≈ 1) variants. The Semitic family exhibits the largest error bars overall, indicating high variability, with mBERT-L2 reaching approximately 15. Bars are not sorted by height within each group, and no visual emphasis such as shading or annotation is applied.
